scope: Full finite-dimensional, all-finite-time ridge-regression confidence event under the manuscript actual conditional sub-Gaussian noise, predictable design, positive ridge/noise/budget and true-parameter norm assumptions. Arbitrary finite coordinate type and arbitrary measurable probability sample space. The formal theorem allows delta>0, extending the manuscript 0<delta<1 case with potentially trivial coverage when delta>=1.

checks.finding: designGram is the sum of rank-one regressor outer products; responseVector sums response-weighted regressors; ridgeMatrix=gamma I+designGram; ridgeEstimate is its actual inverse times responseVector; weightedNorm is sqrt of the actual quadratic form.

checks.claim: Actual Gaussian law and exact determinant formula
checks.finding: The prior is volume.withDensity of the explicitly normalized density. Integral normalization derives IsProbabilityMeasure. Spectral diagonalization plus real Haar coordinate transport and completed-square integrals prove the determinant ratio and inverse quadratic, rather than postulating them.

Each deterministic exponential coefficient has its own a.e. conditional inequality. Finite simple-function approximation and nonnegative Fatou limits derive arbitrary predictable multipliers, then nonnegative truncation derives unbounded predictable wealth factors. No uniform uncountable null-set hypothesis is introduced.

Each literal finite product is adapted and integrable by derived weighted-factor bounds. Joint measurability and product-measure integrability derive the probability-mixture supermartingale using Fubini. Neither supermartingale status nor the final confidence probability is an input to the regression theorem.

VilleInequality bounds the real ever-crossing event by optional stopping of bounded hitting times and increasing finite horizons. Its measurable complement gives the exact radius pathwise at every natural n. Substitution n=T(omega) covers selected finite times.

Taking the logarithm of the positive determinant-weighted mixture bounds the genuine inverse score norm; ridge_error_identity and the quadratic lower bound V>=gamma I derive the sqrt(gamma) S regularization term.

n counts observations 0 through n-1. n=0 gives the zero ridge estimate and prior mixture one. Empty finite coordinate type is allowed and has determinant one. Positive gamma and sigma exclusions match the manuscript. A parameter bound forces S nonnegative.

RegressionMissingDeterminant uses the actual one-observation one-coordinate zero-score mixture whose square is 1/2; the false square=1 is rejected. RegressionMissingRidgeBias uses zero observations and a nonzero true parameter to reject removal of the bias term. Fresh rejection execution belongs to cumulative verifier.
